newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-KALUWITHARANA FIGHTS REARGUARD ACTION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KALUWITHARANA FIGHTS REARGUARD ACTION.

text.p: Sri Lankan wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana defied the New Zealand attack with a fighting unbeaten half century on Monday as the tourists tried to stave off an innings defeat in the first cricket test.

Kaluwitharana belted his way to an unbeaten 70 off as many deliveries as the tourists went to the tea interval on 220 for six in their second innings, still needing another 144 runs to make New Zealand bat again.
He and Chaminda Vaas had put on an entertaining unbroken stand of 87 for the seventh wicket after Sri Lanka looked likely to collapse when slumping to 133 for six after lunch.

Dropped on two when he offered a return catch to fast-medium bowler Simon Doull, Kaluwitharana treated the bowlers with disdain, raising his fourth test half-century off just 46 balls as he scored six fours and one six.
He deposited offspinner Dipak Patel over the long-on fence to bring up both his own 50 and also the 50-run partnership with Vaas, who was on 28 at the break.
Sri Lanka, who were dismissed for 222 in their first innings when responding to the home side's massive 586 for seven declared, resumed on 37 without loss.
But they lost four wickets in the morning session before skipper Arjuna Ranatunga and Hashan Tillekaratne joined their colleagues back in the pavilion during the second session.
Ranatunga, who was on four when the tourists went to lunch on 102 for four, progressed to 13 before he departed after a stupendous catch by Matt Horne at mid wicket.
Ranatunga tried to smack left-arm spinner Daniel Vettori over Horne but the Otago player showed great athleticism to leap high and snare the ball in his right hand.
Tillekaratne was out 18 runs later as Sri Lanka slumped to 133 for six when he fell victim to a brilliant piece of fielding by 12th man Chris Harris.

Tillekaratne, on eight, dabbed the ball into the on side, and set off for a sharp single. Realising too late that a run was not on, he tried to return to his crease but slipped and was out of the frame when Harris threw down the stumps.
